concepts.title: Core blockage and the Major Accident

body.text: The core blockage DBA postulates a blockage of fuel subchannels or other local faults at full power, resulting in fuel damage.

body.text: The source term assumes all fuel pins in a single high burnup assembly fail.

body.text: A partial flow blockage is evaluated because of the tight spacing of fuel pins, high power density, and high burnup in sodium-cooled fast reactor assemblies.

body.text: This DBA has the maximum core damage and in-vessel release, and it was selected as the Major Accident.

title: Design Basis Accidents
subject: event
intro: DBAs set the design criteria for safety-related equipment. Only safety-related equipment is credited, so every sequence is harder than the DBE it came from.

objectives.text: State the event initiator and safety-analysis assumptions.
Identify the challenged safety functions and acceptance criteria.
Recognize the event from alarms and indications.
Select and apply the appropriate procedure.
Respond to failure of an automatic or mitigating function.
Establish and verify the required end state.
Explain the consequences of delayed or incorrect actions.
Relate operator actions to the event's technical basis.
